nodes.label: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention
nodes.author: Namgyu Ho, Huzama Ahmad, Woosung Koh, Se-Young Yun, Tal Schuster, Cicero Nogueira dos Santos
nodes.rationale: Introduces Declarative Attention (DA), a protocol enabling language models to explicitly declare their attention scope through chain-of-thought reasoning, reducing KV cache reads during decoding while maintaining accuracy.

nodes.label: Declarative Attention (DA)
nodes.rationale: Protocol that partitions LLM generation into three attention modes (global, focus, local) declared as parseable tokens in chain-of-thought, enabling inference engine to construct dynamic attention masks from model's own reasoning.

nodes.label: DA Global Mode
nodes.rationale: Attention mode where model surveys full context to locate relevant information; used for navigation and identification of next segments to focus on.

nodes.label: DA Focus Mode
nodes.rationale: Attention mode where model attends only to named context segments for reasoning over specific regions without full-context cost; used for extracting needed values verbatim.

nodes.label: DA Local Mode
nodes.rationale: Attention mode where model attends only to its own recent output without seeing context; used for self-contained reasoning and answer synthesis.

nodes.label: Magic Chunks
nodes.rationale: Addressable segments of long input context (~2K tokens each), presented as simulated tool-use transcript with segment boundaries aligned to special tokens familiar from post-training.

nodes.label: DA State Machine
nodes.rationale: Runs alongside inference engine, parses mode transitions from model output, and updates attention mask at each decode step by rewriting KV-cache block table.

nodes.label: KV Cache Block-Aligned Masking
nodes.rationale: Applies attention mask at block granularity (16-32 token blocks), rounding kept token spans outward to block boundaries to skip entire blocks and reduce memory reads without kernel modifications.

nodes.label: DA vLLM Integration
nodes.rationale: Custom integration with vLLM through hooks on attention metadata builder, rewriting KV-cache block table per decode step without kernel modifications, compatible with FlashAttention.

nodes.label: DA Roofline Wall-Time Analysis
nodes.rationale: Theoretical framework charging each operation at its hardware ceiling (MFU for compute-bound matmuls, MBU for memory-bound reads) to estimate decode wall-clock time savings in optimized large-batch deployments.

nodes.label: System-2 Sparse Attention
nodes.rationale: Frames DA as explicit reasoning-based sparse attention selection (system-2) contrasted with learned sparse attention methods that infer masks from internal activations (system-1).

nodes.label: DA Benchmark Suite
nodes.rationale: 15 long-context sources spanning single-span retrieval/reasoning and multi-span reasoning tasks from RULER, LongBench v1/v2, LooGLE, and ZeroScrolls, with contexts from 6.4K to 1M tokens.

nodes.label: DA Accuracy Metric
nodes.rationale: LLM-judge-based scoring using Gemini-3-Flash to generate strict acceptance rubrics and Qwen-3.5-4B as judge, achieving Pearson r=0.99 with Gemini-3.1-Pro.

nodes.label: DA Attended Tokens Metric
nodes.rationale: Total KV positions attended during decoding, summed over all decode steps and averaged per response, compared as percent reduction relative to vanilla baseline.

nodes.label: DA Context Segmentation
nodes.rationale: Heuristic-based segmentation targeting ~2K-token segments, splitting at coarsest available boundary (paragraph breaks → newlines → sentence ends → clause ends → word boundaries) to align with semantic content.

nodes.label: DA Segment Formatting
nodes.rationale: Presents segments as simulated tool-use transcript with get_magic_chunk tool calls and responses, placing segment boundaries on special tokens (user/assistant/tool message delimiters) familiar from post-training.

nodes.label: DA Zero-Shot Elicitation
nodes.rationale: DA works on off-the-shelf models without parameter updates through single task-agnostic protocol, representing lower bound with significant headroom for post-training optimization.

nodes.label: DA Protocol Adherence
nodes.rationale: Focus success rate (fraction of focus calls resolving to valid chunk references) rises with model size from 58% (Gemma-4-E4B) to 99% (Gemma-4-31B), indicating protocol adherence is dominant bottleneck only at smallest scale.

nodes.label: DA Mode Share Analysis
nodes.rationale: Global mode accounts for ~27% of generated tokens on Gemma-4-31B, while focus and local modes account for ~73%, with global share rising to ~45% at longest contexts.

nodes.label: DA and Speculative Decoding Synergy
nodes.rationale: DA and speculative decoding reduce complementary parts of decode latency; DA lowers per-step KV read cost while speculative decoding collapses sequential steps, with savings stacking since verification passes use masked KV.

nodes.label: Reversible Context Compaction
nodes.rationale: DA enables dynamic KV cache offloading and restoration without re-prefill, as out-of-focus segments can spill to host memory and be prefetched when declarations name them, supporting reversible context compaction.

nodes.label: DA Context-Length Scaling
nodes.rationale: DA's relative accuracy holds within ~1pp of vanilla up to 32K tokens then declines modestly; absolute token savings grow sharply with context (1M at short context to 21M at longest), scaling with raw context length.

nodes.label: DA Model Capability Scaling
nodes.rationale: DA's relative accuracy improves consistently with model size (29% at Gemma-4-E4B to 99% at Gemma-4-31B), narrowing gap to vanilla; token savings roughly scale-independent at ~50% on five of six models.

nodes.label: Lightweight Scan Sparse Attention
nodes.rationale: Existing sparse attention methods that score compact surrogate of every context token at each step; DA proposes synergy where such methods serve global steps while DA declarations carry savings in focus/local modes.

nodes.label: DA Thinking Mode Limitation
nodes.rationale: Models failed to follow DA protocol within thinking traces in preliminary experiments; all results use non-thinking mode, but future work could expose DA operations as standard tool declarations for interleaved thinking.

nodes.label: Global Attention Dominance in Decode
nodes.rationale: Global attention KV reads dominate decode time (73% on Gemma, 86% on Qwen) in optimized large-batch deployments, making DA's per-step masking savings significant and context-length dependent.

nodes.label: DA Relevance in Agentic Systems
nodes.rationale: In agentic systems, context grows incrementally through tool calls; DA addresses complementary problem to retrieval by deciding what model attends to among already-entered context, with savings largest as context accumulates.

nodes.label: Segment Boundary Alignment
nodes.rationale: Aligns segment boundaries with special tokens (user/assistant/tool message delimiters) seen throughout post-training, enabling models to track boundaries fluently rather than arbitrary novel delimiters.

nodes.label: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention
nodes.rationale: Proposes Declarative Attention (DA), a method where language models control their own attention through generated tags, enabling efficient long-context inference by masking KV cache reads.

nodes.label: Declarative Attention (DA)
nodes.rationale: Protocol where models emit <focus>, <global>, and <local> tags to control attention scope, making attention selection explicit and reversible.

nodes.label: vLLM
nodes.rationale: LLM serving system used for efficiency evaluation and integration of DA and Random Attention methods.

nodes.label: Roofline Model Analysis
nodes.rationale: Performance modeling technique used to estimate decode wall-time and show attention dominates at scale.

nodes.label: DA Achieves Efficiency Through Masking Without Scanning
nodes.rationale: Key insight that DA's O(1) mask resolution from generated tags avoids the O(N) scanning cost of learned sparse attention methods.

nodes.label: DA Masking is Reversible
nodes.rationale: Design property that DA masks are reversible (can switch from <focus> to <global>), preserving full cache and enabling re-attendance.
